To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) nonalcoholic fatty livers disease is a cause of type 2 Diabetes, (2) type 2 Diabetes is a consequence of nonalcoholic fatty Liver disease, (3) both are consequences of insulin resistance, (4) both are consequences and risk factors for cardiovascular disease.

NAFLD is strongly associated with the development of insulin resistance and diabetes; however, the molecular mechanisms linking NAFLD with insulin resistance and type diabetes are complex and remain to be fully elucidated.

1) NAFLD is associated with an increased risk of type 2diabetes; 2) hepatic steatosis is associated with insulin resistance, and 3) hepatic steatohepatitis and fibrosis are associated with progressive liver damage.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the pathophysiological mechanisms underlying the association between type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and NAFLD, with the aim of developing new diagnostic and therapeutic approaches to improve patient care and outcomes.
the role of the liver in the regulation of whole‐body glucose homeostasis.
the role of the liver in the development and progression of type 2 Diabetes and its complications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NAFLD is an important early predictor of and a risk factor for type 2 diabetes.
NAFLD is an early marker for the risk of developing type 2 diabetes in patients with insulin resistance and the MetS, but it may not be an independent cause of type 2 DM.
NAFLD is neither a cause nor a consequence of type 1 diabetes, but it may be both in type 2 diabetes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NAFLD is an early predictor and determinant for the future development of type 1 diabetes, but is not a causal factor for type 2 diabetes.
, while NAFLD is not a cause of type 2diabetes per se, it is a marker of insulin resistance and a predictor of the future development of diabetes and its chronic cardiovascular complications.
NAFLD is an early and reversible predictor of the development of type‐2 diabetes, but that it is not a necessary cause of type‐2 Diabetes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the development of insulin resistance in the setting of obesity and the metabolic syndrome is the primary determinant for the development and progression of NAFLD, type 2 diabetes mellitus and other chronic metabolic complications.
the pathogenesis of type 2 diabetics is not a simple consequence of hepatic fat accumulation.

, in the context of insulin resistance and metabolic syndrome, hepatic insulin resistance and excess fat deposition in the liver are likely to be early and independent predictors of progressive liver disease, whereas the development of overt type 2 diabetes depends more on peripheral insulin resistance and impaired glucose disposal.
